episodes.184572: A cold front pushed into Arkansas with high temperatures ahead of the boundary that created the scenario for large dewpoint depressions to create an environment for downbursts to occur across central and push into southern Arkansas.
episodes.184755: A line of showers and thunderstorms moved into northern Utah during the evening hours, resulting in isolated instances of strong wind gusts before dissipating.
episodes.184841: Upper disturbances moving through the moist and unstable air mass produced strong to severe thunderstorms over portions of Lake Superior from the evening of the 5th into the morning of the 6th.
episodes.185162: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the northwestern and central parts of Central Alabama during the afternoon of September 6th. One storm quickly developed over Walker County just after 3 pm, producing damage in the city of Jasper.
episodes.185238: Scattered thunderstorms developed across northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 5th, as a cold front moved through the area. The strongest thunderstorms produced large hail up to half dollar size, and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185239: Scattered thunderstorms developed into far northwestern Arkansas during the late evening of the 5th, as a cold front moved through the area. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185283: An isolated severe storm produced hail up to quarters in size. This was associated with a storm system that developed in the plains and moved into Missouri.
episodes.185322: A relatively weak shortwave rotated over the Great Lakes during the day, setting up unidirectional southwest flow amidst a moisture-rich environment that allowed for multiple clusters of thunderstorms to track over areas near Grand Traverse Bay. There storms produced very efficient rainfall over several hours during the afternoon, leading to multiple reports of flooding and measured rainfall totals exceeding 7 inches in Leelanau county.
episodes.185529: A slowly advancing cold front, roughly paralleling the Interstate 44 corridor, helped initiate widely scattered convection during early evening hours on the 5th. While very hot surface temperatures aided in the development of significant convective (and downdraft) potential instability, weak deep-layer wind shear fostered primarily disorganized (single-/multi-cellular) convection. Downburst wind events, including a cluster of such events just east of the Oklahoma City Metropolitan area, were noted with the most robust convection during the evening.
episodes.185530: A slowly advancing cold front, roughly paralleling the Interstate 44 corridor, helped initiate widely scattered convection during early evening hours on the 5th. While very hot surface temperatures aided in the development of significant convective (and downdraft) potential instability, weak deep-layer wind shear fostered primarily disorganized (single-/multi-cellular) convection. A downburst wind event was noted with the most robust thunderstorm across northern Wichita County.
episodes.185565: Isolated severe thunderstorms developed across portions of the Concho Valley and Heartland producing damaging winds. Also, a significant microburst occurred in Taylor County on September 5th.
episodes.185633: A storm system brought damaging winds to portions of central Missouri. More isolated convection developed across southern Missouri producing isolated wind damage.
episodes.185861: A cold front pushed across north Mississippi during the late afternoon and early evening hours on September 6, 2023.  Thunderstorms initially developed along and south of Interstate 40 as the airmass became unstable and wind shear aloft increased due|to a mid-level jet maximum approaching the region. Thunderstorms became more numerous as the front pushed into north Mississippi, eventually forming a line with several reports of damaging wind and a few occurrences of large hail.
episodes.185971: Convection developed along a quasi-stationary surface front extending from Central and Southwest Arkansas into Southeast Oklahoma on September 6th. Ahead of this activity, low-level lapse rates continued to steepen with rich pre-frontal boundary-layer moisture (mid to upper 70s surface dew points) in place. While large-scale ascent was generally lacking across the region, strong surface heating and destabilization amid the low-level frontal circulation further supported additional convective initiation along the front with a belt of moderate northwesterly mid-level flow over the frontal zone (around 30 knots of bulk shear). This resulted in some weakly organized thunderstorms after updrafts became established and sustained with the threat of isolated large hail and damaging wind gusts. One report of large hail up to quarter size was received in De Queen in Sevier County.

While large-scale ascent was generally lacking across the region, strong surface heating and destabilization amid the low-level frontal circulation further supported additional convective initiation along the front with a belt of moderate northwesterly mid-level flow over the frontal zone (around 30 knots of bulk shear). episodes.186089: On the evening of September 5th, storms brought large hail to portions of western MO.
episodes.186170: A disturbance in northwest flow aloft triggered a round of severe thunderstorms as it interacted with a hot and unstable air mass over southeast Arkansas. These thunderstorms produced some wind damage in far southeast Arkansas.
episodes.189400: Lake Erie, northern OH, and northwest PA resided in a warm and very humid air mass during the late morning through early evening of the 6th as a cold front approached slowly from the western Great Lakes. A line of multicell thunderstorms persisted eastward along a pre-front surface trough axis and generated gale-force peak wind gusts along the northeast OH and northwest PA shore as the storms encountered moderate MUCAPE, DCAPE, and effective bulk shear, respectively.
episodes.189401: Northwest PA resided in a warm and very humid air mass during the late morning through early evening of the 6th as a cold front approached slowly from the western Great Lakes. A line of multicell thunderstorms persisted eastward along a pre-front surface trough axis and generated localized straight-line convective wind damage in the Erie area as the storms encountered moderate MUCAPE, DCAPE, and effective bulk shear, respectively, in northwest PA.
